text: The Hamiltonian has been described as the generator of time evolution. It's also, simultaneously, the energy observable — and those two roles turn out to be the same role, not two coincidentally related ones.

Take the same Hamiltonian from last lesson, h-bar omega over 2 times Pauli-Z. Since Z leaves ket-zero unchanged and flips the sign on ket-one, multiplying through gives H ket-zero equal to positive h-bar omega over 2 times ket-zero, and H ket-one equal to negative h-bar omega over 2 times ket-one. So ket-zero and ket-one are this Hamiltonian's energy eigenstates, with energies plus and minus h-bar omega over 2 — a gap of h-bar omega between them.

If a system starts in an energy eigenstate like ket-zero, time evolution only adds a global phase — invisible, so its measurement probabilities never change, no matter how much time passes. That's exactly what 'stationary state' means: probabilities frozen in time, even though the state vector is technically rotating in phase. Contrast that with ket-plus, which is not an energy eigenstate of this Hamiltonian — last lesson showed it picks up an observable relative phase over time, precisely because it mixes both different-energy eigenstates, and their phases drift apart at different rates.

This isn't just a toy example — it's the standard simplified model for why a physical qubit's two logical states correspond to two distinct energy levels of a real system, separated by a real energy gap. That gap sets a physical control frequency, literally the frequency of the microwave or laser pulses engineers use, and that frequency sets how fast gates can physically run — real tradeoffs between gate speed, qubit stability, and noise trace directly back to this energy structure.
Next lesson closes the loop: showing explicitly why every quantum gate — Hadamard, CNOT, the Pauli gates — is physically a unitary matrix, because a gate IS engineered time evolution.
